problems.title: Three multiplication identities
problems.question: Expand (a) $(a-2b)^3$; (b) $(x^{2k}+x)^2$; (c) $(x^3-c^2+3y)(x^3-c^2-3y)$.
problems.idea: Use exact identities or triangle relations and justify each transformation.
steps: For (a), substitute u=a, v=2b. For (b), square both terms and add twice their product. For (c), first treat x³−c² as one term, then expand its square.

problems.title: Exterior angles reveal a short leg
problems.question: In a right triangle two exterior angles sum to 240°. The shortest leg plus the hypotenuse is 54. Find the median to the hypotenuse.
problems.idea: Use exact identities or triangle relations and justify each transformation.
formulas: The two corresponding interior angles sum to $360°-240°=120°$. The remaining interior angle is 60°.
steps: The triangle is 30°–60°–90°. Its shortest leg is half its hypotenuse c, so c+c/2=54 and c=36. The median from the right angle is half the hypotenuse.

problems.title: Factor three expressions
problems.question: Factor (a) $-2a^2+4ab-2$; (b) $7a^2-7ab+7b^2-a^3-b^3$; (c) $2a^2-6b+a^3-3ab-ca^2+3bc$.
problems.idea: Use exact identities or triangle relations and justify each transformation.
formulas: Use a common factor; $a^3+b^3=(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2)$; grouping gives $2(a^2-3b)+a(a^2-3b)-c(a^2-3b)$.
steps: In (a), factor out−2; the remaining polynomial is not generally a perfect square. In (b), group the quadratic factor common to 7(a²−ab+b²) and a³+b³. In (c), factor out a²−3b.

problems.title: A 120-degree bisector equals a side difference
problems.question: In ABC, A=40°, B=120° and |AC−BC|=8. Find the bisector BD from B.
problems.idea: Use exact identities or triangle relations and justify each transformation.
formulas: The third angle is 20°. Since B is largest, $AC>BC$. Choose E on AC with $CE=CB$.
steps: Triangle BCE is isosceles with apex angle 20°, so its base angles are 80°. Hence ABE=120°−80°=40°, equal to BAE; therefore BE=AE. The ray BD is 60° from BC, so EBD=80°−60°=20°. Since E, D lie toward C on AC, BED=80°, making BDE=80° and BD=BE. Thus BD=AE=AC−BC.

problems.title: Minima from sums of squares
problems.question: Minimise (a) $x^2-6x+2035$; (b) $2x^2+10xy-8x+25y^2+215$.
problems.idea: Use exact identities or triangle relations and justify each transformation.
steps: Squares cannot be negative. For (a), the square vanishes at x=3. For (b), both vanish when x=4 and y=−4/5. Hence both lower bounds are attained.

problems.title: A polynomial identity parameter
problems.question: Find A so $(x-2)(x^3+2x^2+4x+A)=x^4-16$ for every x.
problems.idea: Use exact identities or triangle relations and justify each transformation.
steps: Compare coefficients with x⁴−16. The x-coefficient must be 0, giving A=8, and then the constant is −16 as required.

problems.title: A fixed angle between two bisector feet
problems.question: In triangle ABC, B=120°. Internal bisectors BD and CK meet sides AC and AB at D, K. Prove ∠DKC=30°.
problems.idea: Use exact identities or triangle relations and justify each transformation.
formulas: Write $A=2u$, $C=60°-2u$, so $0<u<30°$. Let $a=BC,b=CA,c=AB$. The bisector theorem gives $AD=bc/(a+c)$, $AK=bc/(a+b)$; hence $AD/AK=(a+b)/(a+c)$.
The sine rule is $a/\sin A=b/\sin B=c/\sin C$. The sum identity is $\sin p+\sin q=2\sin((p+q)/2)\cos((p-q)/2)$. Triangles with an equal included angle and proportional adjacent sides are similar.
steps: By the sine rule in ABC, this ratio is [sin 2u+sin 120°]/[sin 2u+sin(60°−2u)]. Use sin p+sin q=2sin((p+q)/2)cos((p−q)/2) to simplify it to sin(60°+u)/sin(60°−u).

A triangle with angles 2u,120°−u,60°−u has exactly this ratio of the sides opposite its last two angles, since sin(120°−u)=sin(60°+u). Its included angle 2u and the adjacent-side ratio match triangle ADK, so the triangles are similar. Therefore angle AKD=120°−u.
In triangle AKC, angle AKC=180°−2u−(30°−u)=150°−u. Ray KD lies inside that angle, so DKC=(150°−u)−(120°−u)=30°.
